headline: The SCEP client can reach a CA through an authenticating forward HTTP proxy.
summary: Every pki.scep network verb accepts opts.proxy to reach an https CA through a forward HTTP proxy that demands authentication. pki.transport opens a CONNECT tunnel to the proxy and negotiates the origin TLS inside it under the identical trust policy, so the proxy relays the enrollment without seeing it and cannot substitute the origin certificate. A 407 Proxy Authentication Required is answered with Basic (RFC 7617) or Digest (RFC 7616) proxy credentials. A malformed proxy option, a failed CONNECT, or a credential the proxy rejects fails closed with a typed error. Off by default, so the default client is a direct connection.

Added: pki.transport gains forward HTTP proxy support: request.proxy = { url, auth? } opens a CONNECT tunnel to an http proxy and negotiates the origin's TLS inside the tunnel under the same trust anchors and rejectUnauthorized as a direct connection, so the proxy relays the encrypted origin session without visibility into it and cannot substitute the origin certificate. A 407 is answered with Basic (RFC 7617) or Digest (RFC 7616) proxy authentication over the CONNECT request; with blockPrivateAddresses the address guard applies to the proxy hop.

pki.scep threads opts.proxy through every network verb (getCACaps, getCACert, getNextCACert, enroll, renew, getCert, getCrl), so a SCEP enrollment reaches an https CA through an authenticating proxy. A malformed proxy option (scep/bad-proxy), a non-2xx CONNECT (scep/proxy-connect-failed), a 407 with no usable credentials (scep/proxy-auth-required), and a credential the proxy rejects (scep/proxy-auth-failed) each fail closed. An https proxy URL and a plaintext-http origin are not supported in this release and are refused (scep/proxy-unsupported-scheme, scep/insecure-url).
